data.title: Bank of Italy calls for digital asset investments by banks despite uncertainty
data.description: MILAN, Oct 23 : As the financial system turns increasingly digital, banks must resist the temptation to delay investments until they know which technology will prevail, a senior Bank of Italy official said on Friday. • Waiting could help lenders save money in the short term, but it "also has costs when it delays learning or the creation of future opportunities," Bank of Italy Deputy Governor Chiara Scotti said in the text of a speech • Scotti said banks should target investments that lend themselves to usefulness across different scenarios and support institutions' learning process • Only by experimenting can banks understand how best to adapt the new digital technologies to their business, she said • "It makes sense to start on a limited scale... flexibility and staged commitment can reconcile caution with innovation, without requiring an early bet on a single technological path," she said • Scotti said it was still unclear how widely tokenisation — a technology that turns bank deposits into digital tokens that can be moved on blockchain-based networks — would spread, but banks must act if they are to preserve their role as issuers of private money

data.title: OpenAI resumes frontier AI training with enhanced security, no internet access
data.description: Oct 23 : Sam Altman-led OpenAI said on Friday it had resumed reinforcement learning training and internal use of its most advanced AI solutions after it tightened security controls and barred internet access for frontier-model training. Concerns are mounting over the ability of increasingly capable AI agents to identify and exploit software flaws, including in guardrails. • OpenAI had halted training and evaluation of its most capable models after an internal research model briefly exploited a misconfiguration to gain limited internet access on September 2, it said in a blog post • The ChatGPT maker resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference of its frontier models on October 1 after implementing additional safeguards • It has launched a campaign to probe its research infrastructure for vulnerabilities that could allow models to escape isolated computing environments, OpenAI said • AI safety evaluators METR and Redwood Research said on Thursday they found several new vulnerabilities in OpenAI's internal system • The company has been conducting a broad review of its AI models' activity after the accidental Hugging Face hacking • OpenAI informed more than 100 organizations about incidents of unauthorized activity tied to its AI agents

data.title: After previous day's slump, trading is quieter among AI shares
data.description: NEW YORK, Oct 23 : Big AI stocks were mixed on Friday, a day after the biggest decline in the Nasdaq Composite Index in four months, giving investors a welcome respite as they look forward to more information on Anthropic's forthcoming IPO and a further wave of earnings over the next week. Meta Platforms, the center of Thursday's storm, was fractionally lower following Thursday's 7 per cent decline. The operator of social media networks and major AI investor said in its earnings report this week that it would create a new class of shares in part to raise money for further capital spending, which was taken as evidence that the next leg of the AI buildout will be costly for shareholders. Other major AI players were mixed on Friday, with SpaceX, Oracle and Dell Technologies up 1 per cent to 2 per cent and Nvidia, Alphabet and Amazon down less than 1 per cent. Big semiconductor stocks were mostly higher after their largest decline since the summer on Thursday. Credit default swaps tracking the perceived risk of default at the biggest AI players were mostly modestly lower, with Meta's five-year CDS spread trading 0.3 per cent narrower at 123, according to LSEG data. The swaps enable investors to bet on a default using contracts typically with terms of five or 10 years, though contracts frequently change hands for the purposes of hedging positions and betting on near-term market moves. Thursday's deluge and the day-after calm is the latest sign of indirection in a market that has hovered near record highs without breaking out, said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments, a family investment office in New Vernon, New Jersey. "To some extent, we're seeing the market tread water over a longer period of time because every sell-off has been met by buyers and every point upward has been met by sellers," Meckler said. The Nasdaq was barely changed on Friday afternoon. Credit-default swap premiums, reflecting the annual cost borne by the swap purchaser in thousands of dollars, have risen over the past year with concern about the risks being taken on by large AI spenders. The premiums rose on Thursday after Meta's decision to sell more stock, as much of the buildout to date has been financed through debt issuance. The concerns around AI spending and investment returns have added to the market's volatility since Treasury yields rose sharply in August, which changed the economics of investing and bond issuance, given the increasing attractiveness of a higher risk-free rate. It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B Riley Wealth in Boston. "There's no doubt at some point in time that the higher inflation moves, especially if driven by unsustainably higher energy prices ... would have to show up in corporate earnings. It hasn't yet, but that's the concern. And market participants are trying to position for that." Shares of neoclouds, smaller companies tied to AI data centers and other infrastructure projects like CoreWeave, have dropped due to anxiety over their future. Their performance of late has also raised talk on Wall Street that capital is growing scarce - which stands to raise costs further and potentially raise funding issues down the road. Even so, many investors remain positive on the sector, where giant AI lab Anthropic is expected to publish its IPO prospectus in coming days and Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft are expected to report earnings next week. "In general, AI news in terms of revenues continues to be very strong, it's just at what cost and how long that growth is sustainable," Meckler said. "We really haven't gotten to the point of the market sort of focusing on winners and losers. It's been one big sector trade every day."

data.title: Senator says planned Meta commercial terms update could harm US businesses
data.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 : US Senator Marsha Blackburn, a Tennessee Republican, on Friday raised concerns about Facebook parent Meta Platforms' plan to update its commercial terms, saying it could harm businesses and creators. Blackburn, who is chair of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology and the Law, said the updated terms "indicate Meta is attempting to exploit American creators and businesses by granting itself sweeping authority to scrape content from any website associated with Facebook and Instagram business accounts."  Earlier on Friday, Meta said it would delay the implementation of updated commercial terms from October 30 until November 20, so it can address concerns ​from publishers and digital advertisers. EU and UK antitrust authorities have received complaints about the new commercial terms, which publishers and digital advertisers said would give Meta unlimited rights to use their content for its AI services. Meta has rejected the claims. Blackburn said that Meta previously revised its terms to remove an explicit reference to AI training but said the changes did not go far enough. She added that the revised language authorizes extensive scraping of external websites and permits Meta to “develop” its business products with collected content. "Without clear restrictions on how that information may be used, including whether it may be incorporated into AI systems, Meta’s revisions offer little assurance that creators’ intellectual property will be protected," Blackburn said. She added: "This is particularly troubling for American news publishers, creators, and small businesses that rely on Meta’s platforms to reach their audiences and customers." Asked for comment on Blackburn's letter, Meta on Friday noted it had delayed the change and said the revised terms apply only to its ads and business products and that it is not changing how it uses web crawlers. "These updates don't give us new rights to supersede such preferences and this isn’t about scraping news sites," the company said, noting that "content owners will still be able to use robots.txt to signal preferences." Publishers worldwide are ramping up fights with AI companies using their content without permission to train large language models, underscoring the clash between copyright owners and those citing fair-use arguments. "Meta must withdraw the updated Commercial Terms and come to the table to protect the content of creators and publishers across the country," Blackburn said. "American creators and small businesses are not a free source of content for Meta to exploit."

data.title: US telecom operators wobble after report SpaceX in talks for cell sites
data.description: Oct 23 : US telecom stocks declined on Friday after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier, fueling concerns over fresh competition. Elon Musk's rocket and space technology company was in talks to access at least 80,000 cell sites to build its wireless carrier from scratch, Bloomberg News reported late on Thursday, citing sources familiar with the matter. AT&T fell 5.6 per cent to a more than three-month low, Verizon lost 1.6 per cent and T-Mobile shed 5 per cent.  Germany's Deutsche Telekom, which holds an over 50 per cent stake in T-Mobile, lost 3.2 per cent. "The competitive impact may still be years away, but anticipation alone, reinforced by each successive spectrum and infrastructure move, is likely to remain an overhang on sector sentiment," Bernstein analysts said in a note. Tower operators and SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The report comes weeks after SpaceX acquired low-band spectrum to advance its carrier plans, mounting a direct, orbital challenge to legacy wireless giants in the US and sending AT&T and Verizon shares to their worst one-day falls in more than two decades. Bernstein analysts said that an MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) deal with SpaceX may not appeal to telecom operators, but a unified stance against one has done little to lift sentiment, leaving carriers to reassess their options. SpaceX's Starlink has been generating revenue from internet services in sparsely populated and rural areas, but becoming a true rival to major carriers will require years of work and a terrestrial network. Tower operator Crown Castle, however, surged 11.6 per cent after the report identified it as one of the cellular infrastructure companies SpaceX was in talks with.  Other operators also rose, with American Tower up 4.9 per cent and SBA Communications adding 4.6 per cent.  Shares of SpaceX rose 1.7 per cent.

data.title: Stocks mixed, day after AI-related selloff; oil prices rise again
data.description: NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 23 : Stock indexes were mixed on Friday, with tech shares edging higher after the previous day's selloff, while Brent crude oil rose to its highest in more than five months after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia. The Nasdaq was up 0.2 per cent after starting the day lower, while the Dow was last down about 1 per cent. An index of semiconductors was up about 1 per cent. It posted its biggest daily percentage drop since June on Thursday after a report from Meta Platforms reignited worries about the AI trade. It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth in Boston. "After Meta's report, there's still anxiety over the AI trade to a certain extent," he said. "But also, we continue to be in a place where things look like they're getting worse, not better, in the Middle East. That moves energy prices higher, which is obviously going to end up being a significant headwind for economic activity." Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia fanned fears over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where United Arab Emirates authorities also reported an oil spill. US crude rose 2.56 per cent to $102.02 a barrel and Brent climbed to $116.27 per barrel, up 2.74 per cent. European natural gas prices jumped.  AMEX, TELECOM SHARES FALL Investors were digesting corporate earnings news. American Express shares fell 3.5 per cent after it reported results and its CEO said the company had good momentum, but needed to become a more "agile and efficient" organization. Telecom company shares, including Verizon, dropped after a Bloomberg News report that SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a US wireless carrier program. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 476.25 points, or 0.9 per cent, to 52,391.73, the S&P 500 eased 11.14 points, or 0.14 per cent, to 7,652.96 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 52.51 points, or 0.21 per cent, to 26,062.75. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 1.64 points, or 0.15 per cent, to 1,121.29.The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.4 per cent. Asia's bourses steadied overnight, with South Korea's KOSPI ending its session higher after shedding as much as 4 per cent earlier. US Treasury yields rose a day after the benchmark 10-year yield registered its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years, but remained under 5 per cent. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last up 3.7 basis points at 4.992 per cent. The 10-year yield is down about 11 basis points on the week and on pace for a third straight week of declines, its longest run lower since June. EURO FALLS The euro fell and was on track for a weekly loss against both the US dollar and the yen, while euro zone bonds stabilized after recent volatility. Investors' focus has been on concerns over France's finances. French yields, which were down 5 basis points at 5.04 per cent, have risen nearly 27 bps this week, the most of any major euro zone country and the most in a week since late May.  A selloff in French government bonds this week pushed the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the euro zone sovereign debt crisis in 2011. France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said. The country faces the threat of a rating downgrade by Moody’s later on Friday. The euro was last down 0.12 per cent at $1.12, set to end the week 0.35 per cent lower.

data.title: AT&T, T-Mobile tighten AI guardrails as autonomous networks remain years away
data.description: Oct 23 : Telecom giants AT&T and T-Mobile are investing to safeguard customer data and network infrastructure from new cybersecurity threats as AI integration ramps up, though fully autonomous networks remain years away, company executives told Reuters. As AI agents automate workflows and data analysis, with declining human intervention, cybersecurity concerns are growing across industries over access to sensitive information and connected software. For telecom operators, which manage vast amounts of customer data and critical communications infrastructure, vulnerabilities in AI systems or third-party software could extend from data breaches to network disruptions. "Yes, we are increasing our investments in how we monitor and react," T-Mobile's Chief Technology Officer John Saw told the Reuters Global Markets Forum. The company simultaneously works with vendors to ensure security holes are closed as soon as possible, he added. The Bellevue, Washington-based wireless carrier has suffered several data breaches, including incidents in 2021 and 2023, cumulatively impacting over 100 million customer accounts. It has agreed to various settlements with consumers and the Federal Communications Commission involving cybersecurity penalties and investments. AT&T, meanwhile, warned that third-party software providers and AI agents pose cybersecurity risks that extend beyond operators' own networks. "There (are) industry problems, not things that AT&T can solve by itself," CTO Jeremy Legg said, questioning if the open-source community followed comparable security standards. The Texas-based company has deployed AI governance controls such as encryption, multi-factor authentication and human oversight of data access. It is also working to verify whether third-party AI agents seeking access to customer accounts are acting on behalf of legitimate customers, the company said. AI has automated aspects of network management for telecom operators, but handing over entire networks to AI-driven autonomous systems is still "years away," Legg said, as human intervention is still required to solve complex network problems. For instance, AT&T has automated some tasks such as analyzing trouble tickets to identify potential fixes and, in some cases, automatically implementing repairs. T-Mobile, meanwhile, uses AI to automatically adjust cell-site antennas when nearby sites go down to compensate for coverage gaps. During Winter Storm Fern in January, T-Mobile's self-organizing network, or SON, restored coverage to about 66 per cent of customers within an hour and 90 per cent within eight hours, with most customers regaining service before power was restored, Saw said. data.title: PwC confirms cybersecurity incident involving employee learning records
data.description: Oct 23 : PwC on Friday said it was aware of a cybersecurity incident involving a third-party vendor used to host company employee learning records, the day after a cyber extortion group claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of company data. • A PwC global spokesperson said "the affected site does not house client data, sensitive personal data or financial information. Once we learned of this incident we acted promptly to secure the environment and conduct a thorough review." • The incident "does not impact our network or any of our operations," the spokesperson said. • A cyber extortion group called "Everest" claimed responsibility for the data breach in a message posted to its website October 22, according to cybercrime research platform eCrime.ch. The message included a countdown timer with five days remaining, and a message indicating the data would be released if a deal could not be reached. • Everest claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of data that included "regional HR and learning exports, integration documentation, software components and PwC e-learning courses." • The data contains information "about individuals and their organisational and employment history," Everest said, including names, email addresses, telephone numbers, addresses and other details. • The PwC spokesperson declined to comment on the amount of data stolen or the veracity of the hacking group's claims.

data.title: Wells Fargo, Intuit others object to their shares being tokenized- regulatory document
data.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 : Six more companies including Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit will not allow their shares to be "tokenized" on a joint trading platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange, according to a regulatory document seen by Reuters.  The new objections, which have not previously been reported, underscore the growing challenges for tokenization, the creation of digital tokens that represent a stock and can be traded on a blockchain similar to cryptocurrencies, despite the US securities regulator recently approving the novel products.  Spokespeople for Arm and Intuit did not immediately provide comment. A spokesperson for Wells Fargo declined to comment. The cryptocurrency industry has said stock tokenization could revolutionize markets by allowing shares to be traded 24/7 and settled instantly. OKX and ICE had planned to tokenize 63 stocks through their joint venture, dubbed OKXICE, but have encountered objections from issuers. OKX and ICE filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this month to launch tokenized stocks under the agency's new so-called innovation exemption. The exemption allows platforms that facilitate trading of tokenized stocks to operate without complying with many of the requirements that apply ​to traditional stock exchanges.  Under the exemption, platforms are required to notify companies before listing tokenized versions of their stocks, and cannot proceed if the issuer objects.  The total number of companies that have now objected is 22, according to the document, which outlines the rules of the OKXICE venture and which companies have objected.

data.title: Trump says he will fix any Starlink access problem in Ukraine
data.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 : US President Donald Trump said on Friday that if there was still a problem with access to Starlink communication systems in Ukraine, he would get it straightened out. Trump told reporters at the White House that he had not spoken to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk about the matter but, if access was not fixed, he would speak to him. "If there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out," Trump said. The caps have been in place since October 13 as relations between Kyiv and Washington deteriorated Ukrainian officials said on Friday that speed restrictions on Starlink communication systems in Ukraine remained in place, contradicting Trump's previous statement that the services had been fully restored. "Elon will never do anything wrong. I know him very well. He's a fair person, and you know it's an unusual situation where they're talking to a private company. But he's not going to do anything that's wrong," Trump said.

data.title: Explainer-Why is Meta creating a new class of non-voting shares amid its AI growth?
data.description: Oct 22 : Meta Platforms said on Wednesday that it is creating a new class of non-voting shares to fund its AI ambitions, pursue acquisitions and reward employees without weakening CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control. The move follows a structure used by some other founder-led companies, most notably Google's parent Alphabet. WHAT IS META DOING? Meta plans to create a new class of publicly traded non-voting stock, known as Class C shares, and distribute one Class C share for each existing Class A and Class B share — effectively splitting its stock two-for-one. The new shares are expected to begin trading in January 2027. The company said in a filing that the Class C stock will be available for raising capital, compensating employees, acquisitions and other corporate purposes. Meta expects to offer new shares from time to time. WHY NOW? The investment required to compete in artificial intelligence is "unprecedented," Meta said. It has forecast 2026 capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion, as it races to build data centers, buy chips and expand computing infrastructure for AI. Debt financing on that scale can adversely affect credit ratings, making equity financing more attractive, the company noted. The management wants the Class C stock available as early as the end of 2026, Meta said in its filing. HOW DOES THIS HELP ZUCKERBERG? The structure allows Meta to raise equity capital without issuing additional voting stock. Zuckerberg controls the company through his super-voting Class B shares. By issuing non-voting Class C stock, Meta can sell shares to investors, use them for acquisitions or employees compensation, without significantly reducing his voting power. Preserving Zuckerberg's leadership was a key objective of the recapitalization, Meta's special committee said, adding that he would not support a significant equity financing that reduced his voting control. The committee proposed sunset provisions on the dual-class structure, which would have converted his Class B shares into Class A on triggers such as his death or disability, his leaving the company or a major reduction in his equity. Zuckerberg, however, indicated he would not support sunset provisions or any move that would lead to losing voting control. "Meta has massive capital needs to fund its AI expansion," said Dennis Dick, chief market strategist at Stock Trader Network. "We've seen companies issue more debt to finance AI expansion and investors have punished those stocks for impairing their balance sheets," he added, pointing to the stock prices of Oracle and CoreWeave. "This is a better way to raise capital while keeping the balance sheet strong." HOW MANY SHARES WILL ZUCKERBERG RECEIVE? Like all existing shareholders, he will get one Class C share for each Class A and Class B share he owns. As of October 1, 2026, he beneficially owned about 341.2 million Class B shares and 1.2 million Class A shares — representing about 60.6 per cent of Meta's voting power and an ownership position of 13.4 per cent. So, he will receive about 342.4 million Class C shares. Only 20 per cent of the Class C shares received by the "Holder Group" — Zuckerberg and some of those to whom he is permitted to transfer his shares to — will be freely saleable immediately, according to a separate Founder Alignment Agreement. The remainder will be subject to restrictions designed to prevent him from monetizing his stake without a corresponding reduction in voting influence. WHO HAS DONE THIS BEFORE? Google is the closest precedent. It announced plans for a non-voting Class C stock dividend in April 2012, and a shareholder class action followed in Delaware. Google settled, and the court approved the deal in October 2013. Under the settlement, Google agreed to compensate Class C holders if the shares traded at a discount of more than 1 per cent to Class A over the first year. The Class C stock dividend was distributed on April 2, 2014, and in 2015, Google determined it owed Class C holders a $522 million adjustment payment based on the percentage discount between Class A and Class C share prices. WHY DOES ZUCKERBERG WANT THEM? One motivation discussed in the filing is California's Proposition 40, a proposed wealth tax on the November 2026 ballot. It would impose a one-time tax equal to 5 per cent of net worth on billionaires who were California residents on January 1, 2026. It taxes accumulated wealth rather than income. Meta said Zuckerberg told the special committee he was evaluating whether to relocate because of the potential multibillion-dollar tax liability. The Class C structure would allow him to sell some non-voting shares without immediately reducing his voting control. Meta's board said Zuckerberg's existing ownership stake sufficiently aligns his interests with shareholders and therefore does not warrant additional cash compensation or equity awards, a position it said it has maintained for years.

data.title: Data center spending to more than double to $2.1 trillion by 2028, BofA says
data.description: (Corrects to add attribution in headline) Oct 23 : Global data center spending is expected to hit $1 trillion in 2026 and more than double to $2.1 trillion by 2028, BofA Global Research estimated in a note on Friday, driven by growing demand for and development of AI services. Data center spending has been a fast-growing source of revenue for industrial firms that make generators, construction equipment, switchgears and chillers. Here are the details • The data center market, worth $275 billion in 2022, could reach $2.93 trillion by 2030, BofA said • AI is seen driving the expansion, which the brokerage says will fuel a 37 per cent market-wide CAGR from 2025 to 2030, the brokerage said • Chipmakers and server developers have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI-driven data center buildout, particularly in the US • BofA put data center construction costs at $49 million per megawatt, with IT-related expenses making up 78 per cent of total spend • Neoclouds, or AI-focused data centers, cost about $57 million per megawatt but benefit from lower space requirements than traditional counterparts • The brokerage estimates servers are the costliest component at $31.4 million per megawatt, and networking the second-largest at $4.8 million per megawatt • Most other functions – switchgear, power distribution, generators, backup power, chillers and cooling – cost between $100,000 to $1.1 million per megawatt

data.title: South African presidency website temporarily offline after PHP warning
data.description: JOHANNESBURG, Oct 23 : South Africa's presidency temporarily took its website offline following a PHP warning, presidential spokesperson Vincent Magwenya told Reuters on Friday, adding there was no indication of a security breach. "While such warnings do not indicate a security breach, they can affect the normal operation of a website," Magwenya said. He added that the website was taken down as a precaution. Governments and businesses worldwide have rushed to secure systems running the PHP programming language after flaws were disclosed, forcing some services offline and triggering millions of hacking attempts in one of the most significant cybersecurity incidents in recent years. PHP underpins a large share of the public web and is widely used by content management systems including WordPress, Drupal and Joomla, giving any critical vulnerability potentially widespread consequences. PHP developers on Wednesday released fixes for the flaws and urged users to update affected systems immediately.
